# Chichén Itzá Walk

> Independent visitor guide to Chichén Itzá, Yucatán, Mexico. Practical, up-to-date (2026) advice on tickets and the two entry fees, opening hours, the best time to go, day trips from Cancún, Tulum, Playa del Carmen and Mérida, and what each monument means — plus a self-guided offline audio walk by TouringBee. Available in 8 languages: English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Polish and Russian.

This site is a TouringBee project. It is independent and not affiliated with INAH, the government of Yucatán or the administration of the Chichén Itzá archaeological zone. Some links are affiliate links (Tiqets, GetYourGuide, Booking.com, TouringBee); they never affect what is recommended.

## Key facts (2026)

- Entry for foreign adults: about 697 MXN total (~€35 / $40) — one ticket at one window since the Boleto Único replaced the two-counter system in spring 2026 (INAH federal 105 MXN + Yucatán state 592 MXN). Set yearly.
- Opening hours: 8:00–17:00. Ticket booths close and last entry is 16:00.
- Climbing El Castillo and the other structures has been banned since 2006.
- The equinox serpent shadow on El Castillo appears around 20 March and 22 September, in the late afternoon.
- Chichén Itzá is Maya, not Aztec. The Toltecs took the city from the 10th century and built the northern monuments.
